rules.title: Annual Rent Increase Cap (CPI-based, max 4%)
rules.quote: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI 15 months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.
rules.summary: Rent increases are limited to the percentage increase in the CPI-U for the New York–northern New Jersey–Long Island area (15 months prior to 3 months prior to increase), with a maximum cap of 4% per year.
rules.coverage_text: All multiple dwellings as defined in subsection 19:2-2 are subject to Rent Control.
rules.exemption_note: Exemptions include public housing, hotels/motels for transients, commercial rentals, newly constructed multiple dwellings for up to 30 years or amortization period (whichever is less), vacant dwellings substantially rehabilitated (5 years), and units under certain governmental contracts.
rules.penalty: Violations punishable by fine of not less than $100 but not exceeding $2,000 or imprisonment for not more than 90 days or both; Municipal Court may impose additional monetary penalty not to exceed $2,000.

rules.title: Frequency Limit on Rent Increases
rules.quote: The rents for any housing space shall not be increased more than the percentages stated above in any consecutive twelve-month period irrespective of the number of different tenants occupying the housing space during the twelve-month period, any change of ownership of the landlord or vacancy of the housing space.
rules.summary: Rent for any unit may not be increased more than once in any consecutive twelve‑month period, regardless of tenant turnover or change of ownership.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to any housing space subject to rent control.

rules.title: Substantial Compliance and Registration Required for Increases
rules.quote: No annual rent increase, major new improvement surcharge, tax surcharge, or hardship increase is allowed, if the dwelling is not in substantial compliance and/or has not met registration requirements as specified in subsection 19:2-9.8.
rules.summary: No rent increase or surcharge is allowed unless the dwelling is free of code violations and the landlord has registered with the Rent Control Office.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to all dwellings subject to rent control.
rules.exemption_note: Substantial compliance means free from violations of State and Newark health, safety, building, property maintenance, and fire safety codes.

rules.title: Maximum Annual Increase 25% Cap
rules.quote: Since an immediate rent increase of more than 25% above the prior monthly rent may be considered unconscionable and imposes a hardship on a tenant, the Rent Control Board shall not grant increases exceeding 25% in any one year for any tenant.
rules.summary: The Rent Control Board may not grant rent increases exceeding 25% in any one year for any tenant.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to any tenant subject to rent control.

rules.title: New Construction Exemption (up to 30 years or mortgage amortization)
rules.quote: The provisions of the Rent Control Ordinance, which limit the periodic or regular increases in base rentals of dwelling units shall not apply to newly constructed multiple dwellings for a period of time not to exceed the period of amortization of any initial mortgage loan obtained for the multiple dwelling, or for 30 years following completion of construction, whichever is less.
rules.summary: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from rent control for up to 30 years or the amortization period of the initial mortgage, whichever is less.
rules.coverage_text: Newly constructed multiple dwellings with Certificate of Occupancy issued after the effective date.
rules.exemption_note: Landlord must apply to the Board for exemption certification with Certificate of Occupancy before occupancy; exemption period begins on first day of occupancy or 30 days after application, whichever occurs first.

rules.title: Vacant Property Exemption (5 years after substantial rehabilitation)
rules.quote: Dwellings which become vacant and remain vacant for a minimum of 18 months or dwellings which are already vacant on the effective date of this section shall be exempt for a period of five years from any restrictions in the rent that the landlord may charge, if the Rent Control Board determines that the cost of reconstruction or rehabilitation during a twelve-month period has exceeded 50% of the fair market value of the dwelling and that the dwelling has received a Certificate of Occupancy and meets all applicable State and municipal health and housing codes.
rules.summary: Dwellings vacant for at least 18 months are exempt from rent control for five years if the landlord rehabilitates them at a cost exceeding 50% of fair market value and obtains a Certificate of Occupancy.
rules.coverage_text: Dwellings vacant for minimum 18 months and substantially rehabilitated.
rules.exemption_note: Landlord must submit appraisal, rehabilitation plan, permits, and Certificate of Occupancy; application must be submitted within 2 years of acquiring first permit; landlord must notify tenants 90 days before exemption expires.

rules.title: Definition of Rent Includes Security Deposits
rules.quote: Shall mean the consideration and shall include any bonus, benefits or gratuity demanded or received for or, in connection with, the use or occupancy of housing space or the transfer of a lease of such housing spaces, including, but not limited to monies demanded or paid for parking, pets, the use of furniture, subletting, security deposits and damage and cleaning deposits.
rules.summary: Rent is defined to include security deposits, damage deposits, and cleaning deposits demanded or received in connection with occupancy of housing space.
rules.coverage_text: All housing spaces subject to rent control.
rules.exemption_note: This is a definitional provision included within rent control; state law (N.J.S.A. 46:8-19 et seq.) separately governs security deposit amounts and handling.
